title: Descent of the augmented pulled reduction model
statement: For a coefficient datum and scheme morphism as in [def-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-comparison-data], there are ordinary scalar insertion s, its derived transformation delta, a strict ordinary reduction isomorphism e and a strict derived reduction isomorphism tau. The ordinary maps satisfy the prescribed pure-tensor formulas. On every flat-term K-flat completed-coefficient complex, delta and tau satisfy their universal cochain counit formulas and the target counit is invertible. The full strict augmentation commutes with tau and delta. There is no inverse-limit assertion in this lemma.

source.place: Tag 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), proof of (5); the augmented strict-tower and evaluation normalization of the second paragraph of the current blueprint proof is made explicit.

proof.text: Write $U=g^{-1}$, $R=R_T$, $B=B_T$, $R'=R_{T'}$, $D=B_{T'}$, $C=UB$, $S_n=S_{n,T}$, and $S_n'=S_{n,T'}$. The flatness and quotient assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] give $R\to B$, $R'\to D$ flat, with $B\otimes_RS_n=S_n$ and $D\otimes_{R'}S_n'=S_n'$. The constant-sheaf identifications and exactness of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identify $UR=R'$ and $US_n=S_n'$. Choose a flat-term K-flat $B$-representative $P$ of $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements] for the one-object category. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat], $\operatorname{Res}P$ is flat-term K-flat over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], $M=U\operatorname{Res}P$ is such a representative of $N$ over $R'$, and $Q=UP$ is flat-term K-flat over $C$ (use the transported-ring structural isomorphism $UB=C$). Inverse image here is exact on underlying abelian sheaves, so computes the constant-coefficient derived pullback without boundedness.

Put $F_n=P\otimes_BS_n$, with transition $1\otimes q_{b,a}$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] this strict diagram represents $K_\bullet$. The augmented strict comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-common-quotient-reduction-tower] identifies $\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_RS_n$ with $\operatorname{Res}F_n$. Applying the cochain tensor comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] to constant-coefficient pullback, and then inverse image of this comparison, gives strict isomorphisms
$$c_n:M\otimes_{R'}S_n'\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}'(UF_n).$$
Write $T_n=UF_n$, with its $S_n'$-action and induced $D$-action. Exact finite coefficient pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] shows that $T_n$ represents $Lg_n^*K_n$. These complexes are K-flat over $S_n'$, by the normalization calculation in the adic datum and preservation of K-flatness under finite pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. No assertion that $T_n$ is K-flat over $D$ or $R'$ is needed.

proof.text: To identify this entire augmented diagram with the derived tower pullback, let $J$ be the small category with objects $*$ and positive integers, arrows $*\to n$ and $b\to a$ for $b\geq a$, with the evident composition. Let $A_J$ be the $R$-diagram $R[0]\to S_n[0]$. Choose one strict objectwise flat-term K-flat replacement $V_J\to A_J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements]. The augmented $B$-diagram $E_j=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RV_j)$ maps to $P$ at $*$ and to $F_n$ at $n$, using the strict common-quotient comparison in step 2. These are quasi-isomorphisms because $\operatorname{Res}P$ is K-flat. Every $E_j$ is flat-term K-flat over $B$: write it as $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B(B\otimes_RV_j))$, apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] to $V_j$, and [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] to this tensor. Thus $E_J$ is a resolving-class replacement of the whole augmented reduction diagram, not unrelated choices at its levels.

proof.text:
Put $V_j'=UV_j$, so its augmentations to $A_j'=R'[0]$ for $j=*$ and $A_j'=S_j'[0]$ otherwise are quasi-isomorphisms. Pulling $E_J$ back over $B\to D$ gives the strict diagram
$$Z_j=\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_C(D\otimes_{R'}V_j')),$$
by the ordinary tensor and scalar balancing maps [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Flatness of $D$ over $R'$ and its common quotients from [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] make $D\otimes_{R'}V_j'\to D\otimes_{R'}A_j'$ quasi-isomorphisms, with targets $D$ at $*$ and $S_n'$ at $n$. Since $Q$ is K-flat over $C$, tensoring these maps with $Q$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Hence there is one strict objectwise quasi-isomorphism of augmented diagrams from $Z_J$ to the diagram with source $Q\otimes_CD=g_B^*P$, levels $Q\otimes_CS_n'=T_n$, and quotient augmentation. The finite identification is inverse image of the ordinary balancing map defining $F_n$; exactness of $U$ is [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. This proves that $T_\bullet$ is a compatible representative of $H_\bullet=Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$ by [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. In particular no flatness of $C\to D$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); sites-modules.tex Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat). The quasi-isomorphism test is the K-flat definition applied to the cone.

proof.text: The maps $c_n$ in step 2 are therefore an isomorphism of strict representatives of $\mathcal R(N)$ and $\operatorname{Res}'H_\bullet$; let $\tau$ be its localization. On the sheafified pure tensors of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], $c_n$ sends $x\otimes s$ to the corresponding $x\otimes s$. Both transition composites send $x\otimes s$ to $x\otimes q_{b,a}(s)$. The source map $M\to\operatorname{Res}'(Q\otimes_CD)$ is scalar insertion $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Following it by the pulled-back quotient augmentation sends $x$ to $x\otimes1$ in $T_n$, as does $c_n$ after the quotient augmentation $M\to M\otimes_{R'}S_n'$. These are equalities of maps of strict complexes, including the augmented source. The tensor comparison and common-quotient comparison used in step 2 are exactly the two factors specified for $\tau_n$ in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback): pure tensor formulas; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, proof; quotient and scalar-insertion units as in steps 2–4.

proof.text: For a chain map between flat-term K-flat representatives $P\to\widetilde P$, every displayed comparison commutes with it: on pure tensors both orders give $f(x)\otimes s$, and all maps in $Z_J\to T_J$ are induced by coefficient augmentations. By [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements], pullback carries quasi-isomorphisms of resolving diagrams to quasi-isomorphisms; finite reduction has this property by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The universal resolving-class construction [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], applied also to the augmented indexing category $J$, therefore descends these comparisons and equalities to the derived functors, independently of the representatives. This proves the asserted canonicity and naturality of $\tau$ as an augmented tower comparison, rather than only a collection of isomorphisms after evaluation.

theorem strictModelComparison :
    ∃ (s : ordinarySource d g ⟶ completedModulePullback g d ⋙ res d X)
      (δ : source d g ⟶ completedOrdinaryPullback g d ⋙ (res d X).mapDerivedCategory)
      (e : ordinaryReductionSource d g ≅ ordinaryReductionTarget d g)
      (τ : source d g ⋙ OrderedExchange.reduction d X ≅
        tower d g ⋙ (tres d X).mapDerivedCategory),
      IsOrdinaryNormalized d g s ∧ IsStrictNormalized d g e ∧
      (∀ P : CochainComplex (reductionModules Y (d.completedRing Y)) ℤ,
        CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients.{t + 1, t, t + 1}
          (R := d.completedRing Y) P →
        (∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite.{t + 1, t, t + 1, t + 1}
          (R := d.completedRing Y) (P.X i)) →
        δ.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
            (res d X).mapDerivedCategory.map (completedOrdinaryPullbackComplexCounit g d P) ≫
            (res d X).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
              (((completedModulePullback g d).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) =
          (ordinarySource d g).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map (ordinaryComplexComparison d g s P)) ∧
      (∀ P : CochainComplex (reductionModules Y (d.completedRing Y)) ℤ,
        CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients.{t + 1, t, t + 1}
          (R := d.completedRing Y) P →
        (∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite.{t + 1, t, t + 1, t + 1}
          (R := d.completedRing Y) (P.X i)) →
        IsIso (targetCounit d g P) ∧
        τ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫ targetCounit d g P =
          (OrderedExchange.reduction d X).map
              ((ordinarySource d g).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P) ≫
            OrderedExchange.reductionComplexCounit d X
              (((ordinarySource d g).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex e (.up ℤ)).hom.app P)) ∧
      (∀ K : reductionDerivedCategory Y (d.completedRing Y),
        (OrderedExchange.augmentation d X).app ((source d g).obj K) ≫ τ.hom.app K =
          (OrderedExchange.diagonal (A := A) X).map (δ.app K) ≫
            (diagonalRes d X).hom.app ((completedOrdinaryPullback g d).obj K) ≫
            (tres d X).mapDerivedCategory.map (pulledAugmentation d g K))
